extracted.intended_audience: respondent exporters, petitioners, trade counsel, and Department of Commerce analysts participating in antidumping investigations
extracted.subtask_description: Department of Commerce positions responding to parties' comments on calculation issues in antidumping determinations (dates of sale/shipment, allocation, constructed value, interest, adjustments, verification). Applies DOC regulatory interpretation and verification practice to specific adjustment issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sales documentation and plant order breakdowns as best information available
rubrics_metrics.description: When no individual price or cost of manufacture for an item within a package sale exists, the Department used, as best information available, the price breakdowns in the orders to the plant as the price for the subject item, pursuant to 19 CFR 353.37 (1989).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sales documentation does not provide a separate price/cost for the item under investigation, use any available order-level breakdowns; verify at site. Example: where package included an MTP and a blanking press, and no separate MTP price existed, the Department used plant order breakdowns to determine the MTP price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of sale — basic terms agreed; earlier date for large custom-made merchandise
rubrics_metrics.description: A sale has occurred when all basic terms are agreed upon. For large, custom-made merchandise, the Department favors establishing date of sale at an earlier point in the transaction (e.g., initial order) than for fungible commodities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal orders to the plant or earliest written evidence of agreement may constitute the date of sale when they represent the parties' agreement as to basic terms and no earlier documentation exists. Minor specification changes during production and after delivery do not necessarily alter the basic terms or the date of sale (see prior decisions cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of parent-to-subsidiary service charges (related-party transfers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments made by a parent to a wholly-owned subsidiary that arranges services are considered intra-company transfers of funds, not expenses to the consolidated company; only charges paid by the subsidiary to unrelated transportation subcontractors are deducted as movement charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under consolidated accounting (U.S. GAAP), parent/subsidiary payments are not treated as deductible intercompany expenses for U.S. price adjustments. Verify who actually paid unrelated third parties; only those amounts are deductible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissions — bona fide sales commissions, necessity to consummate sale, and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission offsets are allowed only where payments are bona fide sales commissions (not intra-company transfers), are necessary to consummate the sale, or otherwise meet the regulatory standard; after-sales servicing/transportation-arrangement payments are not treated as commissions unless the intermediary possessed necessary licenses to consummate the sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At verification, the Department will examine whether payments labeled as commissions are in fact intra-company transfers used to pay unrelated contractors. No commission offset is allowed without supporting documentation presented at verification. Compare to precedent (e.g., Large Power Transformers from Japan) when intermediary's role was essential to consummating sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term borrowing rate — include all short-term borrowings (fungibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: All short-term borrowings reported in the company's financial system (including foreign currency loans, Tokkin Money Trust loans, back-to-back purchasing agreements) must be used to calculate the company's short-term borrowing rate because money is a fungible commodity and all short-term borrowings can finance working capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If loans are classified as short-term in company records and verification cannot demonstrate specific separate uses, include them in the weighted short-term borrowing rate. Parties cannot exclude such borrowings absent evidence they were exclusively for investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept revised interest rates if verified (clerical error corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent presents a revised interest rate at verification and the Department finds no discrepancies tracing the reported loans to bank invoices/advice, the revised rate can be accepted and categorized as correction of a clerical error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification tracing of loan documentation is required; absence of discrepancy supports use of the revised reported rate in final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of shipment — use completion-of-shipment as unit date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department treats the date on which shipment of the last part of a multi-part unit (e.g., an MTP) leaves the plant as the date of shipment for the item as a unit, when the shipper and parties consider that date as the shipment conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look to common carrier or related shipper invoices and usual business practice; if carrier invoice is issued at completion, that date indicates shipment completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of package-sale payments — proportionate allocation to package price
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments received for a package sale cannot be attributed to any particular item in the package; payments are allocated to items (e.g., MTPs) according to the ratio of the payment amount to the total package price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When payment chronology or amounts cannot be linked to specific components, perform proportional allocation by price ratios among package items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warranty expense methodology — allocate on anticipated lifecycle claims; separate rates allowed where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: It is reasonable to allocate warranty costs based on total warranty costs incurred on MTPs sold during discrete past periods and to estimate total warranty claims anticipated over the life of the presses; separate warranty expense rates for different size categories (e.g., large vs. medium) are appropriate where warranty services are provided through different organizational structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology should match current warranty costs to the sales to which they relate and reasonably predict future costs; a current-cost/current-sales ratio may not be an accurate predictor. Use verification to confirm inclusion/exclusion of transplant sales in home/U.S. warranty calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising expense allocation — include home-market ad costs where no breakdown provided; end-user advertising not deductible from U.S. price
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company acknowledges that home-market advertising expenses were also incurred on behalf of U.S. transplant sales and provides no breakdown, the Department will base the U.S. advertising expense claim on the total of claimed U.S. and home-market advertising expenses; advertising directed to end-users is treated as indirect selling expense and is not deducted from U.S. price for purchase price transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust advertising expense ratios using total sales revenue in audited financial statements where appropriate. Use 19 CFR 353.56(a)(2) for advertising treatment; verify whether advertising was incurred for end-users or on behalf of purchasers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty drawback — add claimed amounts to U.S. price and to constructed value if not in COM
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will add claimed duty drawback amounts to U.S. price in accordance with section 772(d)(1)(B) of the Act; because these amounts were not included in materials costs in the calculation of COM, the Department also added these uncollected duties to constructed value (CV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure duties are treated consistently between U.S. price and CV; follow statutory provision cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unliquidated U.S. import duty refund claims not allowed absent demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will not take unliquidated duty refund claims into account; respondent must demonstrate that refunds have been or will be received, or show historical grants in full amounts, to allow reduction for claimed refunds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of prior grants or actual receipt of refunds; absent such proof, do not reduce duty paid for a sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include bad debt provision if present in financial statements when calculating CV
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provision for bad debt expense is included in the company's financial statements, the Department will use home-market indirect selling expenses inclusive of bad debt expense in the calculation of constructed value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between provisions included in reported financials and excluded non-operating items; verification should confirm presence of bad debt provision on MOF/audited reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of fixed warranty and technical service expenses as indirect selling expenses (unless binding precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department treats fixed warranty and technical service expenses as indirect selling expenses rather than direct expenses eligible for circumstance-of-sale adjustments; court decisions not yet final are not binding precedent on this matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents citing non-final court decisions will not automatically change Department practice; follow Department's normal policy until a binding decision requires change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalized interest — use average annual short-term interest rates experienced during POI
rubrics_metrics.description: For capitalized interest calculations, the Department used the average of the annual short-term interest rates experienced during the period of investigation as reported in the respondent's consolidated financial statements, considering this to reflect company experience during production periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither petitioners' nor respondents' proposed alternatives (weighted-average interest rate from credit expense or average actual interest cost by asset value) were adopted here; use consolidated statement short-term averages unless better verified evidence exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difmer adjustments require costs specifically tied to physical characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences-in-merchandise (difmer) adjustments must identify costs specifically related to different physical characteristics of the merchandise being compared; netting variable costs or making adjustments not specifically tied to physical characteristics is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If manufacturing costs are not associated with specific physical characteristics or adjustments would require thousands of individual cost associations for complex items, the Department may find home-market merchandise not reasonably comparable and reject difmer adjustments, resorting to constructed value instead. See section 771(16)(c) of the Act for similarity standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallow payment-delay offset for related-supplier grace period representing interest-free financing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department agreed that the payment delay offset should not be included in the calculation of capitalized interest for related-party purchases when the grace period effectively represents an interest-free related-party loan; however, if the portion is small, no adjustment may be made per 19 CFR 353.59 (1989) due to insignificance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess materiality of disallowance; apply 19 CFR 353.59 when considering related-party financing offsets and their effect on CV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include depreciation on idle manufacturing equipment in factory overhead/CV
rubrics_metrics.description: Depreciation expense on idle manufacturing equipment, classified as a non-operating expense on MOF reports but incurred on idle manufacturing equipment, is a manufacturing cost and is included in constructed value calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify classification on MOF/cost reports and include such depreciation in COM/factory overhead when it arises from maintaining factory assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include losses on disposal of inventories (obsolescence) as manufacturing cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Losses on disposal of inventories due to obsolescence are considered manufacturing costs and are included in the cost of materials for constructed value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude inventory write-offs from CV if they derive from manufacturing-related disposals; treat as part of material costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offsetting interest income against interest expense and acceptance of post-verification revised calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-term interest income related to operations may be used as an offset to total interest expense. The Department may accept a revised interest calculation submitted after preliminary determination and verification if it is based on data in the original submission and was reviewed during verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisions that are clerical corrections or recalculations based on previously submitted data and reviewed at verification can be used in the final determination; ensure all components were reviewed at verification to avoid introduction of new information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructed value must include home-market selling expenses including imputed credit; circumstance-of-sale adjustments applied after CV
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructed value shall include an amount for general expenses and profit as usually reflected in sales of the same general class or kind (including home-market selling expenses and imputed credit); a circumstance-of-sale adjustment for differing credit terms between home market and U.S. markets is then made after CV is calculated, with imputed home-market credit used in CV and actual finance expenses reduced to avoid double counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute imputed home-market credit based on the terms of home-market sales; reduce actual finance expenses to prevent double counting; follow section 773(e)(1)(b) and precedent cited (e.g., Tapered Roller Bearings from Japan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency conversion: convert at exchange rate in effect on date of sale and use original invoicing currency for incurred charges
rubrics_metrics.description: All conversions of foreign currency into U.S. currency must be made at the rate in effect on the date of sale per section 773(a)(1) and 19 CFR 353.60 (1989). If charges (e.g., ocean freight, marine insurance) were incurred and invoiced in a foreign currency, report them in that currency and convert at the date-of-sale rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not convert yen-incurred charges at the exchange rate on the date the charge was incurred if the invoice indicates charges were incurred in yen and the regulations require conversion at date of sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessory items with segregable prices excluded from scope and CV/COM
rubrics_metrics.description: If an item (e.g., a load meter) is determined not to be within the scope of the investigation because it is an accessory and not an integral part of the basic machine and it has an identifiable and segregable price, its price and manufacturing cost are not included in the subject item's price or cost of manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify scope determinations and whether the accessory has an identifiable/separable price in accounting records; follow DOC positions on what constitutes 'integral' versus 'accessory' components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require supporting documentation at verification for expense claims/offsets
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments such as commissions or claimed offsets will not be accepted if no supporting documentation is provided at verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must produce documentary evidence during verification to substantiate claimed commissions, refunds, or other adjustments; lack of documentation leads to rejection of claimed adjustments.
